facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 土_正印 (Earth carrying The Sage). Persona The Sage (正印). Definition line: "Nourishment that deepens without redirecting, the root that holds". Keyword Care, charge gentle, poles catalyst Wisdom / friction Comfort. Family function: Mind. Cost dimension: the root that holds; shelter that can become stillness. Arena: roots, old trees, the deep well, inherited warmth. Classical portrait: shelter and nourishment that deepens without redirecting; over-protection, "not ready yet" as a place to stay. Ruled domains: Knowledge, Shelter, Nurture. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 偏印.
Element arena: Earth (ground, soil, load, field, bedrock, harvest). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Metal. structural_interaction seed: "Earth generating Metal cross-polarity — stability nourishing precision and opening direction".
- k2_overview: "Your Earth moves as the Sage: mother ground, nurture in its home element, doubled. You hold people the way land holds houses, unconditionally, for generations, without once mentioning the load. Wisdom settles in you and stays. The whole village builds on your patience. Somewhere in the acreage, keep a field that feeds only you."
- k2_functional: "You think in generational wisdom: what held the family, what will hold it next."
- adj_chips: {"friction":["Closed-off","Buried","Unmoving"],"catalyst":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Knowledge":"Your knowledge is settled sediment: practical wisdom layered by years, the kind villages consult. You know what actually works. Write the almanac down. Ground should not be the only copy.","Shelter":"Your shelter is the family land itself: people return to you between every attempt at the world. Being home is holy work with no clock. Post seasons. Even land lies fallow.","Nurture":"The nourishing thread is bedrock here. Where care came early, you draw on it without thinking. Where it was missing, you became the ground yourself. Keep one plot for you."}

- Sibling cell 土_偏印 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Deep-reading","Unhurried","Inventive"],"friction":["Withdrawn","Brooding","Overprepared"]}
- Sibling cell 土_偏印 catalyst row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Taking things in whole is how your mind works, even when the world calls it slowness. You do not sample, you absorb, and what you absorb becomes permanent equipment. Understanding, for you, is not a pass through the material. It is ownership."

Core element Metal, energy element Earth. Law: Earth feeds Metal (土生金: ore grows in the mountain). Relative to the core the energy is the feeder, so Earth is this core's Mind. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Metal core that shows Earth on the catalyst pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The catalyst pole of Earth as the Mind is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: compliment. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 金_土's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: Your presence calms people long before your words do. Since you need the people near you safe more than impressed, you calm them with the slow question ahead of the fast fix. Let someone be the calm one for you now and again, because you need the calming as much as everyone you calm.

value_b.text: You calm people more freely than you ask to be calmed. Calming the people you love is what makes you feel useful, so you play the calm one rather than the one being calmed. Try handing that part over for an evening, because you stay calm for others only by letting someone calm you.

value.text: Knowing what works comes easier to you than hoping something new will. Because you need an answer to have lasted before you lean on it, you reach for what has worked ahead of what sounds clever. Give a new idea one honest try a year, since every answer you trust was new once too.

value_b.text: You keep the answers that have worked and shelve the rest. Knowing what has worked matters to you ahead of knowing what is current, so you change your mind slowly. Let one newer answer in each year, since you pay for the kept ones in chances you never take.

value.text: Whenever a new way shows up, you wait for proof rather than try it. Knowing what works means more to you than being early, so you end up safe and late. Try one untested thing every so often, because you miss the chances that wanted you early by trusting only what has worked.

value.text: You teach a thing a third time in a third way with the patience of the first. You need the person in front of you to get there, so you teach at their pace ahead of your own. Keep one hour a week that teaches nobody, because you alone fill your patience back up.

value_b.text: Teaching at the other person's pace comes naturally to you. Because you put their understanding ahead of your speed, you teach it again rather than teach it louder. Let someone teach you something slowly every so often, since you are owed the same patience you give.

value.text: Teaching someone patiently is easy for you and hard to count. Since you wait for them to get it rather than hurry them, you hand the evening you kept for yourself to the lesson. Say no to one lesson a week, because you take every patient lesson out of your own rest.

value.text: Your patience is the thing you teach with before anything else. You teach it once more instead of watching them struggle, so you take the struggle that would have made it theirs. Let them sit in not knowing a while longer, since you keep from them the practice in every answer you hand over.
